newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent offer slips, other NSea crudes solid.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent offer slips, other NSea crudes solid.

text.p: Dated Brent values slipped on Monday as buyers failed to take on overhang of end-August barrels off the market, traders said.
But other North Sea crudes were firm on a quiet day enlivened by little news.
Intermonth cash spreads weakened marginally from Friday but business was very scanty.
IPE Brent was 22 cents lower on the day at 1715 GMT, pulled lower by U.S. fears of an end to the bull run in the gasoline market.
Short-term swaps drifted a few cents lower at the prompt end while gaining a few pennies on the first two weeks of September the August Brent owner dropped his offer level.

"They are trying to get rid of two end-August cargoes and I've heard they've chopped the offer to October -30 cents," said one trader. Earlier it stood at 20 cents below October but that aroused little enthusiasm.
"They are relatively prompt and I don't see any buyers."
Best bids heard were around the September Brent -35 cents level, traders said, and the anti-Brent mood continued when both Brent dates turning wet on Monday were five o'clocked.
Shell and Sinochem were left with the Sept 2-4 loaders, one of which was a Sept 1-3 deferral.
Other North Sea crudes were steady, underpinned by solid refinery margins in northwest Europe and high freight rates which were seen helping Norwegian offshore loading grades.
A Sept 4-6 Statfjord traded at dated Brent +30 cents and a British and French major swapped a Statfjord and a Forties for dated plus 33 cents and dated plus 35 cts.
Just one contract for difference was heard traded, a Sept 2-8 for October -27 cents, while this week (Aug 18-22) lost two cents to value at October -32/-30, brokers said.
In the Mediterranean, traders said a couple of smaller Urals cargoes were being offered at around Dated Brent -85 cents a barrel, basis cif Augusta, about 10 cents firmer than large cargoes.
"Small cargoes are definitely commanding a premium because there's plenty of competition from Kirkuk for the larger vessels," said one.
Syrian nominations for September had been confirmed but state-owned Sytrol had not yet begun price talks.
"We're expecting a telex from them very soon," said a trader.
Term contract holders are expecting a significant reduction in the official selling price to take account of Iraq's return to the market this month.
"Given that the last Syrian Light traded at OSP -30 cents, the direction should be pretty clear," said one.
